review_state.$comment: V2 Phase 1 addition (BL-012, docs/v2/10-BACKLOG.md), optional/additive. The unified review-state vocabulary means the same thing regardless of how a record arrived (manual intake, import package, or Collector), replacing the V1 split between status and the auto-capture-only validated boolean. The additive rejected value records an explicit human decision on a proposal; it is not published/trusted Evidence. Not required or backfilled onto historical records; status/validated remain the compatibility bridge until Phase 3.

source_tier.$comment: V2 Phase 1 addition (BL-012), optional. Per the blueberry import package's own proposed-schema-enhancements.md P-4: today this only exists informally as a plain string inside `tags` (e.g. "tier-1"), indistinguishable from unrelated tags. Not backfilled from `tags` in this task -- a data-migration concern, not a schema one.

event_date.$comment: V2 Phase 1 addition (BL-012), optional. When the underlying development actually happened, distinct from `captured_date` (when this system captured it) and `published_date` (when it was reported) -- per proposed-schema-enhancements.md P-4. Mirrors `fact.event_date`, added to this repository in an earlier session.

information_confidence.$comment: V2 Phase 1 addition (BL-012), optional. Confidence in the evidence's information itself, distinct from any fact/assessment later derived from it -- per proposed-schema-enhancements.md P-4.

evidence_role.$comment: Optional/additive distinction for long-form and other compound publications. publication_artifact is the whole published item; atomic_evidence is one independently reviewable evidence point derived from a parent Evidence record. Historical Evidence without this field keeps its existing semantics and requires no migration.

parent_evidence_id.$comment: The publication artifact from which an atomic Evidence point was derived. This is Evidence-to-Evidence provenance, not a Source relationship and not a replacement for source_id.

speaker_label.$comment: A publisher/transcript label only; it is deliberately not a Person entity relationship.

artifact_locator.$comment: A precise location in the parent artifact or transcript. start_seconds is sufficient for a point citation; end_seconds provides a bounded segment when known.

extraction_provenance.$comment: How a proposed atomic Evidence point was produced. This does not imply approval; reviewed_by/reviewed_at and review_state record the independent human decision.

transcript_provenance.$comment: Provenance of the transcript material supporting an atomic Evidence proposal. Kept distinct from extraction_provenance because transcript creation and CI statement extraction may use different methods/providers.

transcript_excerpt.$comment: Exact supporting text from the cited transcript segments, retained for human review. This is raw derived material, not the normalized intelligence statement and not automatically trusted.

media_format.$comment: Audio/Video Intelligence data-model foundation phase, optional and additive. How this Evidence record was published -- orthogonal to `source_type` (source_type is the kind of outlet/document, e.g. 'trade_press' or 'patent_record'; media_format is the physical form that document takes, e.g. a trade-press interview could be a web_article or a podcast). Not backfilled onto existing records: their absence of this field means the format was never explicitly captured, not that they are implicitly 'web_article' -- callers must not assume a default. This is deliberately not a new Entity Type: a podcast or video is a form Evidence takes, the same way an Evidence record is not itself a Source (the publisher/outlet/channel that produced it, tracked separately via `source_id`/`source_name`). The enum is the minimum known set for this phase; extending it later (e.g. a distinct 'newsletter' or 'social_post' format) is an additive schema change, not a redesign.

relevance_tier.$comment: Freshness + Company News Recall sprint, optional and additive. Set only on web_article publication drafts that passed relevance screening: 'direct' means a berry species/cultivar or known berry company recurs as a real subject of the piece; 'adjacent' means a genuine strategic-adjacent story (agtech, trade policy, labor, weather/climate) that only mentions a berry once in passing, retained for review but never presented as high-confidence berry relevance. Absent on records this screen never ran against (podcast/video drafts, trusted published Evidence, anything predating this field) -- absence is not evidence of either tier, callers must not assume 'direct' by default.

article.$comment: Article Ingestion vertical slice, optional and additive. The normalized, readable-text body of a web_article Evidence record -- this project's text-artifact analogue of `transcript`, deliberately a separate object rather than forced into transcript_provenance's audio-segment shape (paragraph index is the locator; there are no timestamps for written text). Present only on web_article drafts/Evidence that completed real HTML acquisition; absence does not imply failure -- see `discovery_provenance`/operational run state for why. This is raw derived material carried for human review and later, qualified-model Atomic Evidence extraction -- it is not itself trusted intelligence and `summary`/`why_it_matters` are never overwritten by it.

paragraphs.$comment: Paragraph index is the article's locator, the written-text equivalent of a transcript's segment index -- a future qualified extraction step cites paragraph indexes, never an invented timestamp.

final_url.$comment: Set only when acquisition followed a redirect away from source_url.

acquisition.$comment: Provenance of the article body extraction itself, mirroring transcript_provenance's method/created_by/created_at pattern for the same reason: honest about what produced this derived text and when.

transcript.$comment: Audio/Video Intelligence data-model foundation phase, optional and additive. Metadata describing a transcript's state for podcast/video/conference_video Evidence, ahead of any actual transcription pipeline -- no Whisper integration, no automated generation, and no requirement that any current or future audio/video record have a transcript. Entirely absent on every existing record and on any new record that hasn't had this considered yet; presence of this object does not imply a transcript exists (see `status`).

status.$comment: 'not_available' is an explicit statement (checked, none exists yet); a record with no `transcript` object at all simply hasn't been considered -- the two are deliberately distinguishable.

language.$comment: BCP-47-style language tag (e.g. 'en', 'es'), free-form for this phase.

source.$comment: Provenance of the transcript text itself, mirroring the honesty distinction this project already draws elsewhere (owner claim vs. independent measurement) -- an auto-generated transcript is not the same epistemic weight as a publisher-provided one.

text.$comment: The transcript body, if captured inline. A future transcription workflow populates this; nothing in this phase does.

url.$comment: Link to an externally-hosted transcript, if `text` is not stored inline.
